questions.question_text: Perfume costs $\$157.90$ for $50$ mL. How much does $80$ mL cost?

options.why: Set the equivalent rates up the wrong way round, computing $157.90 \times 50 \div 80$.
Added $\$30$ for the extra $30$ mL, treating the rate as additive instead of multiplicative.
Stopped at the cost of $1$ mL without multiplying by $80$.

questions.question_text: A computer processes $500$ megabytes in $4$ seconds. How long does it take to process $3700$ megabytes?

options.why: Divided $3700$ by the $4$ seconds instead of using the $500$ MB per $4$ s rate.
Found how many lots of $500$ MB there are but did not multiply by the $4$ s each lot takes.
Took the reciprocal in the wrong direction, computing $500 \div 3700 \times 4$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{500\text{ MB}}{4\text{ s}} = \dfrac{3700\text{ MB}}{x\text{ s}}$
$\dfrac{4\text{ s}}{500\text{ MB}} = \dfrac{x\text{ s}}{3700\text{ MB}}$
$x = \dfrac{4}{500} \times 3700$
$= 29.6$
It takes $29.6$ seconds.

questions.question_text: A car uses $9$ L of petrol to travel $100$ km. How far can it travel on $50$ L? Answer to one decimal place.

options.why: Multiplied the $9$ L by $50$ instead of scaling the $100$ km distance.
Scaled from $10$ km rather than $100$ km, so the answer is ten times too small.
Assumed each litre covers $100$ km, ignoring that $100$ km uses $9$ L.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{9\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}} = \dfrac{50\text{ L}}{x\text{ km}}$
$\dfrac{100\text{ km}}{9\text{ L}} = \dfrac{x\text{ km}}{50\text{ L}}$
$x = \dfrac{100}{9} \times 50$
$= 555.6$
It can travel $555.6$ km.

questions.question_text: The water in a reservoir falls from $430\,000$ litres to $180\,000$ litres over $5$ days. At the same rate, how many more days will it take to empty completely?

options.why: Found the rate as $430\,000 \div 5$, using the starting volume instead of the volume lost.
Divided the starting volume $430\,000$ L by the rate instead of the $180\,000$ L that remains.
Assumed the rest of the emptying takes the same $5$ days as the first part.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{(430\,000 - 180\,000)\text{ L}}{5\text{ days}} = \dfrac{50\,000\text{ L}}{1\text{ day}}$
$\dfrac{50\,000\text{ L}}{1\text{ day}} = \dfrac{180\,000\text{ L}}{x\text{ days}}$
$\dfrac{1\text{ day}}{50\,000\text{ L}} = \dfrac{x\text{ days}}{180\,000\text{ L}}$
$x = \dfrac{180\,000}{50\,000}$
$= 3.6$
It takes $3.6$ more days.

questions.question_text: Paint covers $16$ m$^{2}$ per litre. How much paint is needed for three coats on a rectangular wall $5.2$ m by $2.3$ m? Answer to two decimal places.

options.why: Painted one coat only, forgetting to multiply the wall area by $3$.
Used two coats instead of the three the question asks for.
Multiplied the area by $16$ instead of dividing by the $16$ m$^{2}$ each litre covers.

questions.solution_text:
Wall area: $5.2 \times 2.3 = 11.96$ m$^{2}$
Three coats: $11.96 \times 3 = 35.88$ m$^{2}$
$\dfrac{16\text{ m}^{2}}{1\text{ L}} = \dfrac{35.88\text{ m}^{2}}{x\text{ L}}$
$x = \dfrac{35.88}{16}$
$= 2.24$
You need $2.24$ L of paint.

questions.question_text: A car used $30$ litres of fuel to travel $105$ km. Its tank holds $50$ litres. Can it complete a $180$ km journey without refuelling?

options.why: Rounded the rate to $0.27$ L/km before scaling, which understates the fuel and reverses the decision.
Rounded $105$ km to $100$ km, treating the rate as $30$ L per $100$ km.
Set the equivalent rates up the wrong way round, computing $30 \times 105 \div 180$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{30\text{ L}}{105\text{ km}} = \dfrac{x\text{ L}}{180\text{ km}}$
$x = \dfrac{30}{105} \times 180$
$= 51.4$
No. The journey needs about $51.4$ L but the tank only holds $50$ L.

questions.question_text: Fertiliser is spread at $0.2$ kg/m$^{2}$ and sold only in $20$ kg bags. How many bags must be bought to fertilise $750$ m$^{2}$?

options.why: Left the answer as a decimal, but part bags cannot be bought so it must be rounded up.
Rounded $7.5$ down, which leaves $10$ kg of the area without fertiliser.
Gave the mass of fertiliser in kilograms instead of the number of $20$ kg bags.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{0.2\text{ kg}}{1\text{ m}^{2}} = \dfrac{x\text{ kg}}{750\text{ m}^{2}}$
$x = 0.2 \times 750$
$= 150$
$150 \div 20 = 7.5$ bags
Bags cannot be split, so $8$ bags must be bought.
